data.description:
## Context / Problem

`_store/freshness.write_blocking_divergence(tracker)` is the pre-write guard that refuses a ticket write to a tracker with no common ancestor with the shared store. `_commands/_seam._refuse_unpublishable_store(tracker)` passes only the tracker. The function then resolves the code repo from the ambient process (`config.repo_root_or_none()`: `REBAR_ROOT` or cwd) and reads that repo's `tickets_branch` / `tickets_remote` and `git remote get-url`, not the repo that owns `tracker`.

Observed 2026-11-03 while profiling `jobs.run_job` for upset-prissy-olm: a completion-PASS job writing a SIGNATURE event into the op-cert workspace tracker ran `git -C <pytest REBAR_ROOT sandbox> remote get-url origin`, a repo unrelated to the write. The source is `freshness.py:194`, reached from `_seam.py:395`.

Effect: for any write with an explicit `repo_root` that differs from the process root (library callers, the op-cert service workspace, MCP calls with a repo_root), the branch and remote names come from the wrong repo's config. When those names differ, the guard checks the wrong remote ref. It can then miss a real no-common-ancestor divergence, or compare the wrong code remote URL. In the op-cert workspace it happens to be harmless, because the tracker has no remote and the guard returns `None`.

## Approach (proposal)

Thread `repo_root` from `_append_event_body`/`finalize_event` into `_refuse_unpublishable_store`, then into `write_blocking_divergence(tracker, repo_root=...)`, and resolve `base` from it when given. Keep the ambient fallback for callers that pass neither.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test writes a ticket event with an explicit `repo_root` while `REBAR_ROOT` points at a different repo whose `sync.remote` differs. It asserts that `write_blocking_divergence` reads the explicit repo's remote, and no git process runs against the ambient repo.
- [ ] The existing divergence-refusal tests pass unchanged.
data.title: Write divergence guard reads the ambient repo, not the tracker's
